So you want to help write AI policy? Might be good to look back at when it all began...

Watching Congressman Mark Go rise to the podium on August 22, 2023, I couldn’t help but feel the weight of history in the making. I was in the plenary hall... astonishingly more intimate in person than the cavernous space it appears to be on video... and at that moment, the often-abstract debates around artificial intelligence (AI) crystallized into concrete proposals and urgent calls to action.

I must acknowledge the team behind the scenes whose insights shaped the talk points: Oscar Castelo and Mitzi Dupree deserve full credit for their contributions. Their research and strategic framing helped ensure that the speech went beyond grand visions and zeroed in on practical steps for the Philippines to seize the opportunities of AI while guarding against its risks.

AI as a national imperative
Go began by declaring that we stand “at the dawn of a new era,” one defined by boundless possibilities. Too often, AI is dismissed as niche or futuristic, confined to lab experiments or sci-fi scenarios. Yet every day, we interact with discriminative AI... our phones sorting photos, navigation apps guiding us through traffic... and generative AI, from the poems ChatGPT composes to the artwork Midjourney produces. This isn’t tomorrow’s technology; it’s here now.

The promise and the peril
What struck me most was the balanced tone he struck. Yes, AI can automate mundane tasks, unleash waves of innovation, and create new industries. But without foresight, it can exacerbate inequalities... imagine rural communities cut off from reliable internet falling further behind... or fuel a surge of deepfakes and disinformation. Congressman Go’s plea was for “balanced regulation,” legislation crafted not to stifle entrepreneurs but to ensure ethical guardrails and broad access.

Education at the heart
Perhaps the boldest proposal was the campaign to train one million Filipinos in AI fundamentals, mirroring Finland’s celebrated “Elements of AI” initiative. In the plenary, Go invoked the image of our students and workers empowered with the tools to thrive in an AI-driven world. It wasn’t simply about coding bootcamps or elite scholarships... it was about democratizing knowledge so that every driver, shopkeeper, and small-business owner could tap into AI’s potential.

From seed funding to startups
Complementing the literacy campaign, Go proposed a grant facility for AI research and development, urging partnerships between universities, startups, and venture capital. By channeling resources into homegrown talent, the Philippines could avoid being eternally relegated to the role of AI consumer rather than innovator.

Why this speech matters
Congress has debated AI before, of course. But I believe this was the speech that truly got the ball rolling in 2023 during the 19th Congress. The plenary’s modest size did nothing to diminish its impact; rather, it underscored how focused and urgent the conversation had become. In that space, free from the fanfare of large-scale events, policymakers could look each other in the eye and commit to action.

A call to collective responsibility
As I left the chamber that day, I felt both exhilarated and challenged. The work ahead... overhauling curriculum, drafting nuanced data-privacy laws, ensuring equitable internet access... will not be easy. But we need champions like Congressman Go (who ended his term in the 19th Congress) to have the momentum to transform ambition into reality.

In the end, AI is not just a technological frontier; it is a societal one. Our success will depend not only on algorithms and investment but on the collective will of educators, entrepreneurs, and legislators.

Congressman Go's speech is now part of the Congress archive. All its idealism, concepts, promise, now relegated to the a footnote in history. However, if this speech really marked the beginning of the Philippines national AI strategy, then it is really up to all of us to carry the momentum forward... ensuring that when the history of AI in the Philippines is written, August 22, 2023, shines as the day we took one of our first decisive steps.

Now the 20th Congress beckons.

quoted_tweet.text:
So you want to help write AI policy? Let’s start where it began in 2023.

I was in the surprisingly intimate plenary when Congressman Mark Go delivered his privilege speech. 

The energy was electric as the country took its first concrete steps toward national AI strategy. That moment reminded me how education and legislation must move together.

Some of Congressman Go's ideas:
🔥 AI is shaping everything from classrooms to commerce.
📌 We need balanced laws that protect citizens while encouraging innovation.
✅ Training one million Filipinos in AI will empower every community.
🔥 A grant facility for AI R&D can boost local universities and startups.

Now the 20th Congress beckons. Will these ideas come to fruition? Time will tell. 

Let’s prioritize all-of-labor upskilling in AI and train more AI educators... because true progress starts in our schools and training centers.

Naglakad at lumusong sa baha ang ilang commuter sa southbound lane ng SLEX bandang 10:00 PM ng Martes, July 8, 2025, matapos silang ma-stranded sa lugar, base sa mga larawang kuha ni YouScooper Sherilyn Santos.

Ayon kay Sherilyn, sumakay siya ng bus para umuwi sa Alabang nang ma-stranded ang sinasakyan niya dahil sa lagpas sa gulong na baha. Sinubukan din niya umanong bumaba at lakarin hanggang sa tollgate ng Alabang, pero hindi na siya tumuloy. 

Kalaunan, nakauwi rin si Sherilyn matapos lumusong sa baha ang bus na sinasakyan niya. 

Sa abiso ng SLEX-Manila Toll Expressway Systems, Inc ng 12:20 AM, nasa 4.5 kilometro ang tailend ng trapiko mula sa Sucat Exit northbound at nasa 12 kilometro ang tailend ng trapiko mula sa Alabang Exit southbound. #YouScoop

COURTESY: YouScooper Sherilyn Santos
